section.title: Python vs Java — Basics
section.subtitle: Syntax, variables, data types, operators, control flow, collections, functions, exceptions and file handling.

topics.title: Syntax & Variables
topics.learn: How code is written and variables are declared in each language.

python.definition: Python uses indentation (whitespace) to define blocks. Variables are created by assignment — no keyword is needed, and the type is inferred dynamically.
python.code:
# No declaration keyword needed
name = "Alice"
age = 25
price = 19.99

print(name, age, price)

java.definition: Java is strongly typed and statically typed. Every variable needs a type and variables are declared inside blocks delimited by curly braces { }.

topics.title: Print Statements
topics.learn: Outputting text to the console.

python.definition: print() is a built-in function. Multiple values are separated by commas, and f-strings (f"...") embed variables directly.
python.code:
name = "Bob"
age = 30

print("Hello", name)          # Hello Bob
print(f"Age: {age}")            # f-string
print("Age:", age, "years")    # Age: 30 years

java.definition: System.out.println() prints a line. String concatenation uses the + operator; no f-strings exist (use String.format or text blocks).

topics.title: Data Types & Type Casting
topics.learn: Built-in types and converting between them.

python.definition: Python has dynamic typing — a variable's type can change. int, float, str, bool, list, dict, set, tuple are common types. Casting uses int(), float(), str().
python.code:
x = 10            # int
y = 3.14          # float
z = "42"          # str

a = int(z)          # 42 (str -> int)
b = float(a)        # 42.0
c = str(b)          # "42.0"
d = bool(0)         # False

print(type(x), type(y))

java.definition: Java is statically typed — the type is fixed at compile time. Primitive types: int, double, boolean, char. Wrapper classes: Integer, Double, Boolean. Casting uses (type) or parse methods.

topics.title: Operators
topics.learn: Arithmetic, comparison and logical operators.

python.definition: Arithmetic: + - * / // % **. Comparison: == != < > <= >=. Logical: and, or, not. String concatenation uses +.
python.code:
a, b = 10, 3

print(a + b, a - b, a * b)   # 13 7 30
print(a / b)                   # 3.33 (float)
print(a // b, a % b, a ** b)    # 3 1 1000

print(a > b, a == b)            # True False
print(a > 5 and b < 5)          # True
print(not (a < b))              # True

java.definition: Arithmetic: + - * / % (no ** operator). Integer division with / truncates. Comparison and logical operators are the same but use &&, ||, ! instead of words.
java.code:
int a = 10, b = 3;

System.out.println(a + b + " " + (a - b) + " " + (a * b)); // 13 7 30
System.out.println((double) a / b);   // 3.33
System.out.println(a / b + " " + a % b); // 3 1

System.out.println(a > b && b < 5);   // true
System.out.println(!(a < b));         // true

topics.title: If, Else, Elif
topics.learn: Decision-making programs.

python.definition: if / elif / else blocks are defined by indentation. Conditions use ==, !=, <, >, and/or/not.

java.definition: if / else if / else blocks are defined by curly braces. The keyword is else if (two words), not elif.

topics.title: For Loop & While Loop
topics.learn: Repeated operations.

python.definition: for iterates directly over sequences (range, lists, strings). while repeats while a condition is true. Loop variables are implicitly declared.
python.code:
# for loop over a range
for i in range(1, 5):        # 1..4
    print(i)

# for loop over a list
for name in ["a", "b", "c"]:
    print(name)

# while loop
n = 0
while n < 3:
    print("n =", n)
    n += 1

java.definition: for uses C-style syntax: for(init; condition; update). Enhanced for iterates over arrays/collections. The loop variable must be declared with a type.

topics.title: Strings
topics.learn: String manipulation.

python.definition: Strings are immutable sequences of characters. Supports slicing, methods like upper(), split(), replace(), and f-strings for formatting.
python.code:
s = "Hello World"

print(s.upper())          # HELLO WORLD
print(s[0:5])             # Hello (slice)
print(s.replace("World", "Python"))
print(len(s), s.split())  # 11 ['Hello', 'World']

name = "Sam"
print(f"Hi {name}")      # Hi Sam

java.definition: Strings are immutable objects of class String. Methods: toUpperCase(), substring(), replace(), split(). Length via length(). Use StringBuilder for heavy mutation.

topics.title: Lists, Tuples, Sets
topics.learn: Collections — ordered and unordered groups of items.

python.definition: list = ordered, mutable, allows duplicates [ ]. tuple = ordered, immutable ( ). set = unordered, unique items { }. All support len() and iteration.
python.code:
my_list = [1, 2, 3]
my_tuple = (1, 2, 3)
my_set = {1, 2, 3, 3}   # duplicates removed

my_list.append(4)          # [1, 2, 3, 4]
my_list[0] = 10             # [10, 2, 3, 4]
print(len(my_list), my_set) # 4 {1, 2, 3}

java.definition: ArrayList = ordered, resizable list. Arrays are fixed-size. HashSet = unordered unique items. Tuples don't exist; use arrays or List.of().

topics.title: Dictionaries / Maps
topics.learn: Key-value operations.

python.definition: dict stores key-value pairs with {}. Keys must be unique and hashable. Access via d[key], methods: get(), keys(), values(), items().
python.code:
student = {"name": "Priya", "age": 20, "course": "CS"}

print(student["name"])        # Priya
student["age"] = 21            # update
student["grade"] = "A"         # add
print(student.get("missing", "N/A"))  # N/A
print(list(student.keys()))

java.definition: Map<K,V> interface — HashMap is the common implementation. Access via map.get(key), put(key, value). Keys must be unique.

topics.title: Functions
topics.learn: Parameters and return values.

python.definition: def defines a function. Parameters can have defaults and *args/**kwargs. return exits with a value; no return means None.
python.code:
def add(a, b=10):
    return a + b

def greet(name):
    print(f"Hello {name}")   # returns None

print(add(5))        # 15
print(add(5, 3))     # 8
greet("Sam")        # Hello Sam

java.definition: Methods are declared inside a class with a return type. void means no return. No default parameter values — use method overloading or Optional.

topics.title: Exception Handling
topics.learn: Try, except/finally — handling errors gracefully.

python.definition: try / except / else / finally. Catch specific exceptions (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError) or use bare except. finally always runs.

java.definition: try / catch / finally. Catch specific exception types. Exceptions are objects; use try-with-resources for auto-closing.

topics.title: File Handling
topics.learn: Reading and writing files.

python.definition: open() returns a file object — use with for auto-close. Modes: 'r' read, 'w' write, 'a' append. read(), readline(), readlines(), write().
python.code:
# Write
with open("data.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("Hello\nWorld\n")

# Read
with open("data.txt", "r") as f:
    content = f.read()
    print(content)

# Line by line
with open("data.txt") as f:
    for line in f:
        print(line.strip())

java.definition: java.nio.file.Files with Path.of() is modern; older code uses FileReader/FileWriter/BufferedReader. try-with-resources closes files automatically.

topics.title: Exercise: Even or Odd
topics.learn: Practice: check whether a number is even or odd.

python.definition: Use the modulo operator % — a number is even when n % 2 == 0.

java.definition: Same logic — % gives the remainder; even numbers have remainder 0.

topics.title: Exercise: Largest of Three Numbers
topics.learn: Practice: find the largest of three numbers.

python.definition: Compare pairwise with if statements, or use the built-in max().
python.code:
a, b, c = map(int, input("Enter 3 numbers: ").split())

# Using max()
print("Largest:", max(a, b, c))

# Without max()
largest = a
if b > largest: largest = b
if c > largest: largest = c
print("Largest:", largest)

java.definition: Use Math.max() twice, or nested ternary/if comparisons.

topics.title: Exercise: Reverse a String
topics.learn: Practice: reverse a string.

python.definition: Slicing with a negative step s[::-1] reverses a string in one line.
python.code:
s = input("Enter a string: ")
print("Reversed:", s[::-1])

# Without slicing
reversed_s = "".join(reversed(s))
print(reversed_s)

java.definition: StringBuilder.reverse() is the standard way; or iterate backwards.

topics.title: Exercise: Palindrome Check
topics.learn: Practice: check whether a word is a palindrome.

python.definition: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards. Compare s with s[::-1].

java.definition: Compare characters from both ends, or reverse the string and compare with equals().

topics.title: Exercise: Factorial
topics.learn: Practice: find factorial of a number (n! = n × (n-1) × ... × 1).

python.definition: Use a for loop accumulating the product, or math.factorial(), or recursion.
python.code:
import math

n = int(input("Enter a number: "))

# Loop
fact = 1
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    fact *= i
print(f"{n}! = {fact}")

# Built-in
print(math.factorial(n))

java.definition: Use a for loop with a long accumulator, or recursion.

topics.title: Exercise: Prime Numbers
topics.learn: Practice: find prime numbers up to N.

python.definition: A prime has exactly two divisors: 1 and itself. Test divisibility up to sqrt(n).
python.code:
def is_prime(n):
    if n < 2: return False
    for i in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1):
        if n % i == 0: return False
    return True

limit = int(input("Find primes up to: "))
primes = [n for n in range(2, limit + 1) if is_prime(n)]
print(primes)

java.definition: Same algorithm — loop i from 2 to sqrt(n), check n % i.

topics.title: Exercise: Count Vowels
topics.learn: Practice: count vowels in a sentence.

python.definition: Iterate characters, convert to lowercase, check membership in 'aeiou'.
python.code:
sentence = input("Enter a sentence: ").lower()
vowels = "aeiou"
count = sum(1 for ch in sentence if ch in vowels)
print("Vowel count:", count)

java.definition: Loop through chars, use String.contains or a switch on lowercased char.

topics.title: Exercise: Duplicate Elements
topics.learn: Practice: find duplicate elements in a list.

python.definition: Use a set to track seen items; report items seen twice.

java.definition: Use HashSet to track seen; HashSet duplicates for results.

topics.title: Exercise: Simple Calculator
topics.learn: Practice: create a simple calculator.

python.definition: Read two numbers and an operator, use if/elif for each operation.
python.code:
a = float(input("First number: "))
op = input("Operator (+ - * /): ")
b = float(input("Second number: "))

if op == "+": result = a + b
elif op == "-": result = a - b
elif op == "*": result = a * b
elif op == "/" and b != 0: result = a / b
else: result = "Invalid input"

print(f"{a} {op} {b} = {result}")

java.definition: Same approach — switch or if-else on the operator character.

topics.title: Exercise: Student Marks Management
topics.learn: Practice: a student marks management program.

python.definition: Store students in a list of dicts, compute total/percentage/grade, display a report.
python.code:
students = []

for _ in range(3):
    name = input("Name: ")
    marks = list(map(int, input("Marks (3): ").split()))
    total = sum(marks)
    pct = total / 3
    grade = "A" if pct >= 90 else "B" if pct >= 75 else "C"
    students.append({"name": name, "total": total, "pct": pct, "grade": grade})

for s in students:
    print(f"{s['name']}: {s['total']}/300 ({s['pct']:.1f}%) Grade {s['grade']}")

java.definition: Use a Student class with fields, an ArrayList<Student>, and a loop to print the report.
